note.question: How do different purchase options by strategic consumers affect a firm’s profit and the firm’s strategies for the timing and pricing of its successive generations of product diffusion?
note.overview: Frequent new product releases pose significant challenges for firms as they manage successive generations of product diffusion. The paper develops an analytical model to study the effect of different purchase options by strategic consumers on a firm’s profit and the firm’s strategies for the timing and pricing of its successive generations of product diffusion. The paper shows that consumers’ strategic behavior, although adversely affecting the sales of the first-generation product, positively influences the sales of the second-generation product through an initial “seeding” effect.

models.summary: Frequent new product releases pose significant challenges for firms as they manage successive generations of product diffusion. The paper develops an analytical model to study the effect of different purchase options by strategic consumers on a firm’s profit and the firm’s strategies for the timing and pricing of its successive generations of product diffusion. The influence of strategic consumers on profit and sales depends largely on the discount-to-price ratio of the first generation relative to the performance improvement in the second generation.
